newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan urges Cambodia to reverse closure decision.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan urges Cambodia to reverse closure decision.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign ministry on Thursday threatened "drastic measures" against Cambodia if it does not revoke its decision to close Taipei's unofficial trade office there.
"This is completely unacceptable. We have urged the Cambodian side to revoke its decision," a foreign ministry spokesman told Reuters by telephone.

Cambodian co-premier Hun Sen said on Tuesday that Taiwan's office in Cambodia would be closed, alleging that it had been involved in backing forces loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, whom Hun Sen ousted in a coup earlier this month.
Taiwan, the largest foreign investor in Cambodia, has categorically denied any involvement by its government or people in the conflict.
It received notification from Phnom Penh on Wednesday.
"The allegation is groundless. It's ridiculous," the spokesman said.
"We are still awaiting Cambodia's reply today. We will consider taking drastic measures if it does not withdraw its decision," the spokesman said.
He declined to say what measures Taiwan might take.
Cambodia recognises Taiwan's arch-rival, communist China, which has regarded the island as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, and has no diplomatic ties with Taipei.
Hun Sen said Taiwan investors were not involved in the affair and they should continue business as usual.
Earlier, Hun Sen said unidentified Taiwanese, including a general, supported Ranariddh's forces before fighting erupted between troops loyal to the two premiers on July 5.
Hun Sen said Beijing's embassy in Phnom Penh was sufficient to look after the interests of Chinese people in Cambodia.
Taiwan said it did not rule out the possibility that Beijing was involved in Hun Sen's decision.
"It's highly possible. Chinese communists always try to squeeze us on the diplomatic front whenever they have a chance. We don't rule out such a possibility," the ministry spokesman said.
